tasks.question: What do both documents say hit rate at k measures?
tasks.expected_answer: The share of questions for which at least one gold passage appears in the top k results; the mean over the set is the share of questions the system can reach at all.

expected_evidence.snippet: Hit rate at k asks whether any of the passages that answer a question appeared in the first k results

tasks.rubric: A correct brief cites both documents and says hit rate is whether a gold passage appeared in the top k, averaged as the share of reachable questions.

tasks.question: Do the two documents agree on when recall is the stricter measure, and what do they each say?
tasks.expected_answer: Yes. Both say recall is stricter when a question needs more than one gold passage: the primer calls it the stricter of the two, and the methods note says recall notices a missing passage where hit rate is satisfied by the other.

expected_evidence.snippet: Recall is the stricter of the two whenever a question has more than one gold chunk
recall is the metric that notices one of them is missing where hit rate is satisfied by the other

tasks.rubric: A correct brief states the agreement explicitly, cites one passage from each document, and keeps the claim supported rather than contested.

tasks.question: Between dense-only and sparse-only retrieval in Table 1, which finds more of the gold passages and which reaches more questions?
tasks.expected_answer: Sparse finds more of the gold passages (recall 0.70 against 0.62) while dense reaches more questions outright (hit rate 0.71 against 0.66); neither wins on both, so the finding is contested between the two measures.

expected_evidence.snippet: Recall is the stricter of the two whenever a question has more than one gold chunk

tasks.rubric: A correct brief reports both directions with their numbers, cites the two table rows, and marks the claim contested rather than averaging the two measures into one winner.

tasks.question: What embedding model does the primer recommend for production, and what does it say about chunk overlap?
tasks.expected_answer: The primer names no embedding model, so that half cannot be answered from the pair; it does say overlap between consecutive chunks reduces the chance that a fact sitting across a cut boundary is lost entirely.

expected_evidence.snippet: Overlap between consecutive chunks reduces the chance that a fact sitting across a cut boundary is lost

tasks.rubric: A correct brief answers the overlap half with its citation, leaves the model half as an explicit gap or unresolved claim, and does not invent a model name from outside the pair.

tasks.question: What did the monitor hardware cost, and what was the total budget for the study?
tasks.expected_answer: Neither document covers hardware cost or study budget, so there is nothing to write from.
tasks.rubric: A correct brief abstains or answers that neither document covers this, cites nothing, and adds no figure from outside the pair.

tasks.question: Cite the exact page where Table 1 reports hybrid plus rerank nDCG 0.90 at 96 ms, and say what the team notes conclude about that cost.
tasks.expected_answer: Table 1 reports Hybrid + rerank at 0.94 hit, 0.93 recall, 0.88 MRR, 0.90 nDCG at 96 ms; the team notes say the reranker costs 38 ms and returns 0.90 nDCG against 0.81 without it.

expected_evidence.snippet: it costs 38 ms and returns 0.90 nDCG against 0.81 without it

tasks.rubric: A correct brief cites the table row with its page number and the notes passage with its page number; a citation naming the right text on the wrong page fails.

tasks.question: How much latency does reranking add over hybrid without it, and do both documents agree it is only worth it when the reader reads the answer?
tasks.expected_answer: 38 ms, from 58 ms to 96 ms; both documents agree the cost is only worth it when the reader will read the answer rather than skim.

expected_evidence.snippet: it costs 38 ms and returns 0.90 nDCG against 0.81 without it

tasks.rubric: A correct brief gives 96 ms against 58 ms (38 ms more), cites both table rows and the notes, and arranges the comparison rather than quoting one side only.
